paragraphs.source_en: When one comes to speak of teasing people, there is nothing more amusing. Even a cat like me sometimes takes pleasure in teasing the young ladies of my master's household. So it is perfectly natural that the gentlemen of Rakunkan should tease this dull-witted master, and probably the only person dissatisfied with it is the man being teased. If one analyzes the psychology of teasing, it has two elements. First, the person being teased must not remain perfectly calm and indifferent. Second, those doing the teasing must be far stronger than the other side, both in power and in numbers. The other day, after returning from the zoo, my master repeatedly told of something that had greatly impressed him. When I listened closely, it turned out that he had seen a quarrel between a little dog and a camel. The little dog, he said, raced around the camel like a gale, barking furiously as it ran. The camel, however, paid it no mind at all and simply stood there, as before, carrying the great lump of flesh on its back. No matter how the little dog barked or raved at it, the camel would not take any notice, and in the end the dog lost interest and stopped making a fuss. My master laughed and said that camels were truly insensitive creatures. In fact, that incident is the best possible example of the situation involved in teasing. No matter how skilled someone may be at teasing, if the opponent is a camel, the teasing simply cannot get started. Or, to put it another way, if the one being teased is a powerful lion or tiger, the teasing will not work either. The moment you begin teasing it, you will be torn to pieces. Teasing is extremely pleasant only when the other bares its teeth and gets angry at you, yet, though angry, can do nothing to you. Why should teasing of this sort feel so enjoyable? There are various reasons. First of all, it is well suited to killing time. When people are bored, they may even feel like counting the hairs of their own beard. It is said that a prisoner once cast into jail was so overcome with boredom that he spent his days drawing triangle after triangle on the wall of his cell. There is nothing in this world harder to endure than boredom. If there is no incident to stir and excite one's vitality, being alive becomes painful. Teasing, in the end, is a kind of amusement in which one creates such stimulation and plays with it. However, unless one can make the other party somewhat angry, impatient, or distressed, it will not amount to stimulation. Therefore, since ancient times, those who devote themselves to teasing as a pastime have been limited to two kinds of people: either idle persons like foolish feudal lords who never consider anyone else's feelings; or boys whose minds are still immature, who have no leisure to think of anything beyond their own amusement, and who do not know how to spend their energy. Of course, when it comes to proving one's superiority in actual practice, there is also a very simple method. For example, killing someone, injuring someone, or framing someone can all prove one's superiority. However, these are methods adopted with killing, injuring, or entrapping people as their direct aim.

paragraphs.source_zh: 捉弄人这件事说起来是最有趣的。就连我这猫儿，也时常以捉弄主人家里的小姐们为乐趣哩。落云馆的君子们来捉弄这愚笨的主人是完全应该的，而为此感到不满的恐怕只有被捉弄的本人了。如果分析一下捉弄人这一心理，则有两个要素。第一，被捉弄的一方决不可满不在乎，置之不理。第二，捉弄人的这一方，必须是在力量方面、人数方面都远远超过对方。前些日子，主人参观动物园回来，曾反复地讲过一段使他深感佩服的事。仔细一听，原来是他看见了一条小狗和骆驼吵架。据说小狗像疾风一般围绕在骆驼四周，一边跑着一边狂吠。而骆驼呢，则只当没事儿一般，仍然背着它那背上的大肉瘤，站在那里纹丝不动。不管这小狗如何狂吠，如何向它发疯，它就是不予理睬，最后小狗自觉无趣，就不再闹腾了。主人嘲笑说，骆驼这东西真是个钝感的动物。其实，这件事正好可以说明捉弄人这种情况的最好例子。不管对方怎样擅长捉弄别人，遇上对手是骆驼，也就捉弄不成了。或者换句话说，如果被捉弄的对方是力量强大的狮子或老虎，那也就捉弄不成了。你刚一捉弄它，立刻就会被它撕得粉碎。你捉弄它，它龇牙对你发怒，而尽管发怒，但又奈何你不得，只有在这种情况的时候，捉弄才是非常愉快的。为什么说这样的捉弄才感到愉快呢？这里有各种原因。首先，可以消磨时光。人在无聊的时候，甚至会闲得数自己的胡须有多少根。据说过去被投入牢狱的囚犯，由于过分无聊，便每天在墙上重复画三角形混日子。人世上再没有什么比无聊更难使人忍受的了。如果没有什么刺激人的兴奋事件，那么活着是很难受的。捉弄这种行为，说穿了就是制造刺激来游戏的一种娱乐。不过，如果不能使对方多少有所发怒，或有所焦躁，或有所困惑，那么就不成为刺激。所以古时候那些热衷于捉弄人作为娱乐的人，不外乎是两种人，要么是从不考虑别人感情的蠢侯爷这类闲得慌的人；要么是除了自己寻找乐趣之外无暇考虑其他事儿的、头脑还处于幼稚状态、而又不知道怎样消耗自己精力的少年。当然，为了实际证明自己的优势，也有最简便的方法。比如干些杀人、伤人或者诬陷人的勾当，都可以证明自己的优势。不过，这些都是以杀人、伤人、陷害人为直接目的而采取的手段。
